slides.title:
The Shape
of an Idea
slides.copy: How constraints turn possibility into form.

slides.title: What if the blank page is not empty?
slides.copy: Every project begins with boundaries: time, tools, audience, and intent.

slides.title: Three moves
slides.copy: A simple way to make ideas concrete enough to test.

features.title: Shape
features.copy: Use constraints to reveal a direction.

features.title: Test
features.copy: Put the idea where people can respond.

slides.title: More options can mean less movement
slides.copy: When every direction remains possible, no direction becomes real.

features.title: Expand
features.copy: Generate enough range to see the field.

features.title: Choose
features.copy: Name what the work will refuse.

features.title: Commit
features.copy: Give one direction enough time to speak.

slides.title: Constraints are a creative material
slides.copy: They give an idea edges, tension, and a recognizable point of view.

features.title: Time
features.copy: Decide what must be true first.

features.title: Form
features.copy: Let the medium influence the answer.

features.title: Audience
features.copy: Design for a specific moment of understanding.

slides.title: A useful rhythm
slides.copy: Illustrative percentages show how a talk can carry a visual progression.

slides.copy: Turn one vague project into a sequence of answerable questions.

features.title: Write
features.copy: State the decision in one sentence.

features.title: Listen
features.copy: Use the response to shape the next move.

slides.title:

have a shape.
slides.copy: One thought to carry into the discussion.
